source_text: V. Tunc Reno, qui nobiscum fuerat, somno apprehenso, ostensum est ei produci singulos, quibus prodeuntibus lucernae singulae praeferebantur; cuius autem lucerna non praecesserat, nec ipse procedebat. et cum processimus nos cum lucernis nostris, expergefactus est. et ut nobis retulit, laetati sumus fidentes nos cum Christo ambulare, qui est lucerna pedibus nostris et qui est sermo, scilicet dei. VI. Post ipsam noctem dies nobis hilaris agebatur. et continuo eadem die subito rapti sumus ad procuratorem, qui defuncti proconsulis partes administrabat. o diem laetum, gloriam vinculorum! o optata votis omnibus catena! o ferrum honorabilius atque pretiosius optimo auro! o stridor ille ferri qui strepebat dum trahitur per aliud ferrum! loqui nostrum futurorum solatium fuit, atque ne hac iocunditate tardius frueremur, a militibus incertis ubinam nos praeses audire vellet circumducti sumus huc atque illuc per totum forum. tunc nos in secretarium vocavit, quia necdum hora passionis advenerat. unde prostrato diabolo victores sumus in carcerem reversi et ad alteram victoriam reservati. hoc itaque praelio victus diabolus ad alteras se astutias vertit, fame nos et siti temptare molitus, et hoc suum praelium multis diebus fortissime gessit, ita ut (quod magis secum adversarius facere putabat) aegrorum copia ad solonem fiscalem et aquam frigidam laboraret.
pass_a_gloss: Then, sleep having seized Reno who had been with us, it was shown to him that single persons were being led out, and as they went out single lamps were being carried in front of them; but the one whose lamp had not gone ahead, he also did not go forward. And when we went forward with our lamps, he was awakened. And when he reported it to us, we rejoiced, trusting that we walk with Christ, who is a lamp to our feet and who is the word, namely of God. After that night a joyful day was being passed by us. And immediately on the same day we were suddenly seized to the procurator, who was discharging the office of the dead proconsul. O happy day, glory of bonds! O chain longed for by all vows! O iron more honorable and more precious than the best gold! O that grinding of iron which rattled while it was dragged against other iron! Our speaking was a consolation of future things, and lest we enjoy this delight too slowly, by soldiers who were uncertain where the governor would wish to hear us we were led about here and there through the whole forum. Then he called us into the secretarium, because the hour of suffering had not yet come. Hence, the devil having been thrown down, as victors we returned into prison and were kept for another victory. Therefore the devil, conquered in this battle, turned himself to other cunning devices, having endeavored to test us by hunger and thirst, and he waged this battle of his most strongly for many days, so that, as the adversary rather supposed he was doing with himself, a multitude of sick persons struggled toward fiscal allowance and cold water.
pass_b_english: Then Reno, who had been with us, was overtaken by sleep, and it was shown to him that each person was led forward, and as each came forward a single lamp was carried before him; but the one whose lamp had not gone ahead did not himself come forward.
And when we came forward with our lamps, he awoke.
And when he told us what he had seen, we rejoiced, confident that we walk with Christ, who is a lamp to our feet (Psalm 119:105) and who is the Word, that is, of God.
After that night we spent a bright and cheerful day.
And at once, on that same day, we were suddenly hurried before the procurator, who was discharging the office of the deceased proconsul.
O happy day, O glory of our bonds!
O chain longed for by every prayer!
O iron more honorable and more precious than the finest gold!
O that grating of iron as it rang while iron was dragged against iron!

Our talk together comforted us concerning what was to come, and lest we taste this joy too late, soldiers who did not know where the governor wished to hear us led us round hither and thither through the whole forum.
Then he called us into his private hearing room, because the hour of suffering had not yet arrived.
So with the devil cast down we returned to prison as victors, and were reserved for a second victory.

Defeated in this contest, therefore, the devil turned to other wiles and strove to try us with hunger and thirst, and he pressed this assault of his fiercely for many days, so that, as the adversary chiefly intended in his own mind, a crowd of sick men lay suffering on prison gruel and cold water.

lemmas.gloss: the devil having been laid low

choices.why: dative of advantage with pes; keeps the Psalm wording and the dream image of lamps carried ahead
rejected: a light for our path in general

choices.english: the Word, that is, of God
choices.why: sermo here is christological, parallel to lucerna, so capitalized Word rather than ordinary speech

choices.english: he summoned us into his private hearing room
choices.why: secretarium is the magistrate's chamber for preliminary examination, not yet the public tribunal for sentence
